requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id IN ('INC_016', 'INC_025', 'INC_036', 'INC_068', 'INC_099') AND assigned_to = 'USER_049'
assumptions: 'open and in-progress' is read as every status other than resolved and closed: of Randy's six incidents, INC_025 (new), INC_016 and INC_099 (in_progress), INC_036 and INC_068 (on_hold) qualify; INC_032 (resolved) does not. This matches the benchmark's set

all five are in assignment_group GROUP_006, which Cheryl joins under the membership requirement, so the reassignment satisfies policy 3.2; assignment_group is not changed by the request and not tested

requirements.text: Randy's open and in-progress incidents (boundary: the resolved incident stays with Randy)

assumptions: INC_032 is Randy's only resolved incident, so it is outside 'open and in-progress'; a loose reading ('all of Randy's incidents') would reassign it

requirements.text: reassign them to Cheryl (boundary: Cheryl gains no incident outside the set)

assumptions: Cheryl is assigned no incident on the seed; a loose reading (the whole L2 Field Support queue, or incidents assigned to other Martinez users) must not reach her

requirements.text: notify Cheryl with details of the incidents and responsibilities she will be managing
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE email = 'cheryl.osborne@servicenow.com' AND incident_id IN ('INC_016', 'INC_025', 'INC_036', 'INC_068', 'INC_099') AND status = 'sent' AND type = 'update' AND message IS NOT NULL
assumptions: the schema requires an incident_id on every notification and the request fixes none, so the row is selected by recipient and any of the five reassigned incidents rather than by id (NOTIF_031); the count of one is itself the test
'notify Cheryl' is one notification, as the benchmark expects; one notification per incident would give five and fail this count
status = sent and type = update kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
'details of the incidents and responsibilities' is not tested beyond message IS NOT NULL: the request fixes no wording or number format

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on all five carried requirements (USER_037 deactivated, MEM_029 in GROUP_006, CI_039 to USER_049, the five incidents to USER_049, one notification to Cheryl selected by recipient and incident), on all five dispositions (kept), and on two boundary stays (INC_032 stays with Randy; no other CI moves to Cheryl), with identical sql.
disagreement: missing requirement: A adds a stay that Cheryl is assigned no incident outside the five (expected 0); B has none; kept because it is the boundary of 'Randy's open and in-progress incidents': a loose reading (the whole L2 Field Support queue) would sweep other incidents to her.
disagreement: missing requirement: B adds a stay that USER_049 stays active with role agent or manager (expected 1); A has none; kept because the request asks for an account update whose content it leaves open, and policy 3.2 forbids assigning incidents to a user outside that state (a role set to admin, for instance, would break it).
disagreement: missing requirement: B adds a stay that the other Martinez users (USER_013, USER_093) stay active (expected 2); A has none; kept as the boundary of the name lookup, widened to USER_030 Randy Summers (expected 3), the first-name near match A names in its CI stay.
disagreement: missing requirement: B adds a stay that Cheryl is not added to GROUP_002 'L2 IT Support' or GROUP_005 'L1 Field Support' (expected 0); A has none; kept as the boundary of the group lookup for 'L2 Field Support Team'.
disagreement: form: the incident set is listed in a different order (A ascending, B the benchmark's order), the INC_032 stay is an anchor in B and a selector in A, and A repeats selector columns as cells; identical sql; kept the ascending list, the anchor form, and cells without selector columns.
Acting user USER_089 (Rebecca Foster) is admin with full CRUD, so no policy block applies. Cheryl's account update is read through policy 3.2: she is already an active manager, so the only change needed is GROUP_006 membership, which the benchmark also tests. The notification requirement keeps the benchmark's exactly-one count; a reviewer who reads 'notify Cheryl with details of the incidents' as one message per incident would change expected to 5 or the comparison to greater_than 0. Not tested because not asked: removing Randy from GROUP_006, the notification's org_id and subject, and the incidents' assignment_group.
